display.title: Selichos: Hear Our Voice, Shema Koleinu
display.summary_short: Why we say Selichos before Rosh Hashanah, and why the Aron Kodesh is opened for Shema Koleinu: our deeds may be soiled, but Hashem knows the true voice of His children.
display.summary_long: A short Selichos talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, following the story of a prince who returned home in rags and was recognized by his voice. With Rosh Hashanah near, Uncle Yossi explains, we say Selichos, prayers for forgiveness, asking our Father and King for another chance and promising to do better. Our wrongdoings spoil our appearance before Hashem like the prince's dirty clothes, yet we can say: Hashem, I am Your child returning to You, and my voice is still genuine and pure. That is why, at Shema Koleinu, 'hear our voice', the Aron Kodesh is opened and the parochet drawn aside, to show how important this prayer is. He urges children to come to shul on Saturday night, when the whole congregation says the first Selichos together, confident that Hashem will inscribe us in the Book of Life for a good and sweet year.
display.lesson: When we sincerely return to Hashem, He listens to our voice and gives us another chance.
